You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like late 2016, probably the end of October or November.

- **Unemployment and policy rate:** unemployment is 5.0% and fed funds is about 0.37%, which fits mid-2016. The fed funds rate was near 0.37–0.40% in mid-2016 and rose to 0.54% in December 2016.
- **10-year yield:** at 1.84% it is lower than the 2.3% seen in December 2016, so the date is before then. The 10-year was about 1.5% in July, 1.6% in September, and 1.84% in October.
- **Core CPI:** 2.2% year over year fits 2016.
- **Industrial production:** -2.03% year over year fits 2016.
- **Gold:** +5.1% in one month and +15.6% over three months suggests a strong run. Gold rose sharply in June and July 2016 (Brexit), which points to June or July. October 2016 gold fell, so the gold figures argue against autumn.
- **Equities and rates:** the 3-month US equity return is +7.1% and the 12-month return is +1.1%. The 12-month figure fits mid-2016 (June–July 2016 was about +2–3%). The 10-year yield dropped to 1.37% in July 2016, which doesn't match 1.84%.
- **Alternative date:** the data could instead be early 2016 (February), when the 10-year was about 1.78%. But the emerging-market equity 3-month return of +12.5% and gold at +15.6% fit March 2016, when gold rose in Q1 and the 10-year was about 1.78%. At the end of March 2016, fed funds was about 0.36%, VIX was about 13.9, and the dollar was falling. The 3-month change in the 10-year of -0.10 also fits, since the 10-year was 2.27% at the end of 2015. A 12-month emerging-market return of -17.9% fits too. US equity returned +0.4% in 1 month and +7.1% in 3 months (from the February low), which suits March 2016.
- **Payrolls and VIX:** payrolls averaging about 209k fits March 2016. The VIX at 15.2 is close to the March 2016 level.

I'll go with March 2016.
